0: FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 March 1987, after the draft finalized by the Special Alloys Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been prepared for rationalizing the requirements of magnetic materials which are often referred to as `Commercially Pure' or `Magnetically Soft' irons. This material is generally available hot in a wide variety of forms, such as slabs, billets, ingots, forgings, rolled bars or as flat rolled sheets and strips. 0.3 The main applications for these materials are in dc relays, t loudspeakers, electro-magnets, magnetic clutches, brakes, parts for magnetic circuits in instruments and control apparatus as well as for [pole pieces and other tic parts for generators and motors. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, with expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-19tio*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements of cold drawn soft magnetic primarily intended for electroiron rods, bars, flats and sections magnetic applications, such as relay, cores, etc, of electrical machinery and apparatus,

8.6 Tolerance on Length-for-Rods, Bars, Flats and Sections tolerance of fl percent on the length specified will he allowed. extremeties should be clean and free from burrs.

8.7 Tolerance on Straightness of Bars-When placed on a horizontal flat surface and loaded by their own weight only, the maximum deviation from the surface, between two points, at a distance of 1 metre from each other, should be within 1 mm. 8.8 Tolerance on Out-of-Roundness - Out-of-roundness is the difference between the maximum and the minimum diameters, measured at the same cross-section. It shall not be more than half of the tolerance on the diameter. 9. MATERIAL ON COIL

RETEST 11.1 Should any of the test pieces first selected fail to pass any of the tests specified in this standard, two further samples shall be selected, from the same lot one of which shall be from the original strip or coil Should the test ljirces from both for testing in respect of each failure. the addnlonal samples pass, the material represented by I hc test samples shall be deemed to comply with the requirements of that particular Should the test pieces from each of these additional samples fail, test. the material rcprcscntccl by the test sample shall be deemed as not conforming to this standard.

NWI.E - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act lWC_ and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defmcd systctrt of inspection, testing and quality control Standard which is devised and supcrviscd by HIS and operated by the producer. marked products arc also continltoltsly checked by 111s for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Urtails of conditions uncler which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the bureau of Indian Standards.
